outcome.descriptive: The history guard reads a git command where the shell runs it: prose that names an operation is no longer refused, a quoted `<<` no longer hides the command after it, and a quoted heredoc body that cat pipes to a plain script run is that script's input.
outcome.technical: Written by the orchestrator (guard command-reading code). guard-history-rewrite: `_shell_pieces` now lexes with `_op_tokens` (operators only outside quotes, comments dropped), replacing shlex plus `_SEP_SPLIT`, which cut a shell's quoted -c argument at a quoted `<<`/`;` and lost the command after it; `_quoted_substitutions` became `_substitutions` (every $( ) and backquote outside single quotes, since the lexer now keeps a bare one whole inside its word); new `_command_positions` counts a git only at the program word of a command past reserved words, assignments and run-their-argument wrappers (`_config.program_candidates`), fallback candidates included; new `_substituted_command` reads a substitution in command position as running what its body prints; `_printed` reads printf's arguments and its format; new `_is_sourced_at_start` treats a write into a shell/env start-up file (.bashrc, .zshenv, .profile, .envrc, profile.d, fish config) as running it. _config.split_heredocs: a marker counts only where the shell reads one (`_scan_quotes` carries a quote stack across lines; `$(` reopens command context inside double quotes, so the house `-m "$(cat <<'EOF' ...)"` form is still a heredoc); new opt-in `pipe_data` (history guard only, via runnable_text) reads a quoted body that `cat` pipes to a plain script run (`_pipes_to_script_run`, the same `_plain_script_run` rule as the head form) as data, keeping the two holes that removed the earlier far-side reading shut: a second pipe and an interpreter option assigned in the command (NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONINSPECT, PYTHONSTARTUP, PERL5OPT, RUBYOPT) keep the body; any head but bare `cat` keeps it. guard-secrets-read keeps the strict reading (its hp1 unchanged and green). Rows that pinned the old every-word base flipped to allow with new rationale: gp1, gp2, gp3, gp7, gp11, gp17, gp19, gq1, gq2, and test_hooks' unquoted-git-words class (n17b). SECURITY.md: the history-guard paragraph, the piped-body sentence and the residual list rewritten to the command-position reading. New cases: cp1-cp17 (history), hq1-hq8 (config). Before the fix cp1, cp2, cp14, cp15 and hq1, hq2, hq4, hq5 were red; hq6/hq7/hq8 were added after a regression seen in gw14d/gw14e (a heredoc inside double-quoted $( ) must stay a heredoc) and gq27 (an awk head runs the body). Sweep 331/331 files ok, --spaced 331/331, bench-hooks gate ok, ruff and vermin clean.
